html:
The Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA) is a nonprofit founded in 2006 by the Gates Foundation and the Rockefeller Foundation to raise the yields of Africa's small farmers. It is based in Nairobi.

The name looked back to the Green Revolution of the 1960s, when new seeds, fertiliser and irrigation sharply raised wheat and rice yields in Asia and Latin America, work that Rockefeller money had backed. Africa had largely missed it. AGRA set out to help farmers buy improved seed and fertiliser, build seed companies and dealer networks, and push governments toward policies that favour them. Kofi Annan became its first chairman.

Its stated goal was to double the incomes of 20 million farming households and halve food insecurity in 20 countries by 2020. Results were mixed. Studies in the late 2010s and early 2020s found that yields of staple crops rose less than hoped and hunger in its focus countries did not fall as planned. Critics said its focus on bought inputs suited agribusiness more than poor farmers. The group later dropped "Green Revolution" and now goes by AGRA.
sum: The Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA) is a nonprofit founded in 2006 by the Gates Foundation and the Rockefeller Foundation to raise the yields of Africa's small farmers. It is based in Nairobi.
